ledger.note: 1 August 1960: Dahomey becomes independent from France. The country has 'full independence on 1 August 1960' and was called Dahomey after independence.

30 November 1975: Dahomey is renamed Benin ('after the Bight of Benin'), and a self-described Marxist-Leninist People's Republic of Benin 'existed between 1975 and 1990'. The state and its territory continue.

1 March 1990: the People's Republic of Benin becomes the Republic of Benin. The page says the name change 'took effect on 1 March 1990' and that in 1991 the Marxist-Leninist state 'was replaced by the multi-party Republic of Benin'. The territory is unchanged.

certainty.note: Judgment: the page lists neighbours (Togo, Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Niger) but no boundary instrument or dispute; the frontier is inherited from the French colonial delimitation, which the page does not describe. Not a source.

sources.title: Benin
sources.note: Independence 1 August 1960, Dahomey renamed Benin 30 November 1975, 1990 name change, area 114,763 / 112,622 km2, Porto-Novo and Cotonou. Silent on border disputes and on any territorial change.

notes: Budget: 1 page; Benin has no territorial event on the page beyond independence and two renamings. Not settled: the 1961 annexation by Dahomey of the Portuguese fort at Ouidah (Sao Joao Baptista de Ajuda), if the Benin page's silence hides one (a gap-filler should open 'Sao Joao Baptista de Ajuda'); the Benin-Niger frontier along the Niger River (the page is silent on any dispute). The 1961 and 1969 shapes differ by 0.2 percent with no page explanation. Cliopatria's 1960 land sits in the French Fifth Republic row. Neighbours in the seed: Burkina Faso, Nigeria, Niger, Togo.
